messages:
marta: Quick Q re: prefix-cache contract — when we compute the cache key for the text-generation endpoint, are we canonicalizing prompt whitespace & user metadata? A few edge cases from dev-ex: old clients send `prefix` vs `prompt_prefix`, temperature changes, streaming, and how we expose cache headers. TL;DR: want to confirm rules before I update the SDK docs.

kevin: Short answer: yes — we canonicalize prompt prefixes (normalize newlines, trim, collapse spaces) and ignore ephemeral user cookies for shared cache keys. Will expand below.

sam: Which parameters are considered part of the key? temperature/seed/streaming? Need explicit list for backcompat.

jess: From the design doc: key = model + normalized(prompt_prefix) + hash(normalized prompt body) + canonical params (temperature, top_p, stop_tokens) + system_role + rollout_id. Streaming flag is NOT part of the cache key — streaming affects delivery only.

marta: Good — streaming not part of key. What about `prefix` vs `prompt_prefix` param names? Old webhooks still send `prefix`.

kevin: Server maps both to canonical field `prompt_prefix`. For canonicalization: replace CRLF with LF, trim leading/trailing whitespace, collapse multiple spaces to one. Also treat `system_role` case-insensitively. Any other metadata flagged as "sensitive" is excluded from shared key.

sam: How do we signal cache hits to clients?

jess: Proposed headers:
- `X-RW-Cache`: `HIT` | `MISS` | `PARTIAL`
- `X-RW-Cache-Key`: sha256 hex (debug only)
- `X-RW-Cache-TTL`: seconds remaining (debugging aid)
- `Cache-Control`: `public, max-age=<ttl>` OR `private`/`no-store` based on sensitivity

kevin: Note: for privacy-sensitive requests (customer opt-in or user-specific content), we set `Cache-Control: private` and we do NOT write to the shared cache (we return `X-RW-Cache: MISS` and may optionally serve from a per-user cache if enabled).

marta: Invalidation: do we support tag-based purge if a prefix changes?

kevin: Two mechanisms: TTL and tag purge API. We attach tags like `prefix:{sha}`, `model:{name}`, `rollout:{id}` to cache entries. Purge API: `POST /cache/purge` with tags OR `POST /cache/purge/key` for explicit keys. Also model rollouts bump `rollout_id` so old cache entries don't get served once rollout changes.

sam: Backcompat risk: older clients already wrote entries with different normalization — duplicates? Any migration plan?

kevin: We canonicalize on ingress so new requests map to canonical keys. For existing duplicate entries, ops will run a dedupe/backfill job next week that consolidates by `X-RW-Cache-Key` (we'll compare hashes). Also we keep a compatibility layer that accepts `prefix` name to avoid skew.

jess: Implementation snippet for canonical key (for SDK/docs):

```
function canonicalPromptKey(prefix, prompt, opts) {
  const norm = s => s.replace(/\r\n/g,'\n').trim().replace(/\s+/g,' ');
  const normPrefix = norm(prefix || '');
  const promptHash = sha256(norm(prompt || ''));
  const params = ['model','temperature','top_p','stop_tokens','system_role','rollout_id']
    .map(k => `${k}=${String(opts[k] ?? '')}`).join('|');
  return sha256(`${opts.model}|${normPrefix}|${promptHash}|${params}`);
}
```

kevin: We intentionally include `stop_tokens` and `rollout_id` in the params. Don't include ephemeral fields like `request_id` or cookies.

marta: Ops asked if we can add `X-RW-Cache-TTL` header to help debugging — okay to expose?

kevin: Yes for public caches. For private/no-store responses we omit TTL to avoid leaking retention policies.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: cache-service v2 -> canary 10% at 2026-02-15T09:20Z :rocket:

jess: One more corner case: partial cached continuations. If cached output is shorter than requested `max_tokens`, do we mark HIT?

kevin: We mark `X-RW-Cache: PARTIAL` when the cached chunk is shorter than requested continuation. We include `X-RW-Cached-Length` and `X-RW-Required-Length`. Behavior: return cached chunk immediately and compute the remainder online (or fetch from model) — client sees PARTIAL.

marta: Great. I'll update SDK docs to list header enums, canonicalization rules, and backcompat notes (prefix vs prompt_prefix). Will also add examples for `PARTIAL`.

sam: Thanks — I'll sync with devex so examples are in the quickstart. :thumbsup:
